overall.summary: NuScale (SMR) shows a pattern of reducing quantitative specificity in its MD&A disclosures between the Q1 and Q2 2025 10-Q filings. The most concerning changes involve the removal of a $69.3M purchase commitment payment schedule, elimination of financial sustainability language including a $7.4M USTDA contingent obligation, and the deletion of a specific retaliatory tariff risk factor—all occurring during a period of heightened trade tensions and as the company remains pre-revenue and capital-constrained. While several peer comparison flags are false positives due to fundamental business differences, the temporal degradation flags paint a credible picture of reduced transparency on material financial commitments and risks.
